source_evidence: For example, your beneficiary may receive the greater of: (i) all the money in your account; or (ii) some guaranteed minimum, such as all purchase payments minus prior withdrawals.
question: Misconception: A variable annuity’s death benefit always guarantees that the beneficiary will receive all the purchase payments, even if there were withdrawals.
answer: The death benefit depends on the contract. The source says a beneficiary may receive the greater of the account value or a guaranteed minimum, which could be purchase payments minus prior withdrawals. Check the contract’s specific death-benefit terms.
